subject: Science
title: Natural and made materials
objective_verbatim: Group natural and human-made materials; record results in a table (ICT).
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 2.9 on 664 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 8.9 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to sort things from nature and things people make.
success_criteria: I can sort one raw item.
I can sort one made item.
I can add a row to a table.

vocab.definition: from nature, not made into a new item

vocab.example: People make a brick from clay.

vocab.definition: what a thing is made of

worked_example.full: This raw rock is from nature. I write raw rock in the Natural row.
worked_example.faded: People shape and fire clay to make a brick. I write brick in the ____ row.
worked_example.removed_step: Choose Human-made as the group for the finished brick.
worked_example.fade_next: Give the raw and finished item with a blank table; pupil fills both rows.

cfu.question: Is a finished brick raw clay, or an item made by people?
cfu.answer: It is made by people from clay.

hinge.question: People shape sand into a glass bottle. What is the finished bottle?

options.diagnosis: Confuses the source material with the finished object.
Calls a finished item raw at the same time.
Names the finished object as made by people.
Misses the natural or human-made grouping.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on; otherwise re-model This raw rock is from nature. I write raw rock in the Natural row. Ask the parallel hinge. No scores or answers saved.
hinge.parallel_hinge: People cut wood and assemble a chair. Is the finished chair raw wood or a human-made item? A human-made item.

misconceptions.misconception: A made thing is natural whenever its raw material is natural.
misconceptions.correction: Put source clay and finished brick in separate rows.

misconceptions.misconception: A table is only a picture of groups.
misconceptions.spot: Cannot name row and column information.
misconceptions.correction: Point to the item column and group column, then make one row.

we_do.support: Hold a raw rock. Point to its group.
we_do.stretch: Where do raw clay and finished brick go? Why?

tiers.F: Put one raw and one made item in groups. Fill one row.
tiers.M: Sort four items. Add two rows to a table.
tiers.H: Why is clay natural but a brick made?

stems.M: I put ____ in the table as ____.
stems.H: The raw ____ is ____, but the finished ____ is ____.

tiers.go_deeper: An object has two materials. How can your table show both?
tiers.early_finisher: Choose a made item with two raw materials. Plan a fair row.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Give a three-step visual card for natural and made materials; remove its last cue after a correct try.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Point to the real kit before a short spoken, signed or AAC response; wait for a turn.
adaptations.semh: Offer a private first–then cue and planned pause before the hinge; re-enter with one step.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Use a stable tray, large cards or an accessible input; no forced touch.
adaptations.eal: Rehearse a full M or H idea in any language before writing; keep the science challenge.

M.q: Is a finished brick made by people?
M.a: Yes. People make it from raw clay.
What a thing is made of.

H.q: How can clay be natural but brick made?
H.a: Clay is raw material; people shape and fire the brick.

H.q: How can a table show two raw materials?
H.a: Add two material entries for one made item.

facts.claim: Raw rock and a leaf on a branch are natural examples in this simple classification.
Clay is a natural raw material and people shape and fire clay to make brick.
A finished glass bottle is made by people; it is not a raw natural sample.
A table records a group beside an item in a row.
Vocabulary term natural means from nature, not made into a new item; example: A raw rock is natural.
Vocabulary term human-made means made or changed by people; example: People make a brick from clay.
Vocabulary term material means what a thing is made of; example: The brick has clay in it.
Vocabulary term table means rows and columns for facts; example: This row says brick: made.
Retrieval question from SoW C42: Name one use of a rock. Answer: Slate can cover roofs, where suitable.
Retrieval question from SoW C41: What does a water test check? Answer: Whether water passes through the sample.
Retrieval question from SoW C36: What do people and animals get from food? Answer: Nutrition.
The “Raw clay” → “Shape, fire” → “Made brick” labels depict the manufacturing process: people shape and fire natural clay to make a brick.
New transfer hinge and parallel: People shape sand into a glass bottle. What is the finished bottle? Correct: A human-made glass item.

Independent (8 min): Make a row for raw and made items. Staff: Choose one adult for supported pupils, one for group; swap across the week.
